title: Processors run only on the in-process reactor path — the SharedWorker path silently skips every factory
content:
The processor documentation carries an explicit "Not stable yet" warning that is easy to miss and expensive to discover empirically: **processors run only on the in-process reactor path.** On the SharedWorker reactor path, processor registration is not bridged — Connect logs a warning and skips every factory (`apps/connect/src/store/reactor.ts`). Worker-hosted reactors do not run processors today.

The failure mode is the worst kind: silent and total. Nothing throws. Your factory builder is never called, `onOperations` never fires, your relational tables stay empty, and the only signal is a console warning. Anything that depends on a processor — a search index, an analytics rollup, a webhook, a follow-up dispatch — simply does not happen.

This also explains the shape of the registration API. The processor manager is deliberately **not** a method on `IReactor`; it lives on the in-process reactor module as `processorManager`. Reaching it requires narrowing on the module kind, which is the code-level expression of the same constraint:

```typescript
const reactorModule =
  reactorClientModule.kind === "browser"
    ? reactorClientModule.reactorModule
    : undefined;

await reactorModule?.processorManager.registerFactory(id, factory);
```

Note the optional chaining. If the reactor is not on the browser in-process path, `reactorModule` is `undefined` and the `registerFactory` call evaporates without complaint.

Practical consequences while this is unstable:

- Verify which path a host actually booted before debugging a processor that "does not run" — check the module kind, not the processor code.
- Treat processor-mediated behavior as unavailable in worker-hosted topologies, and do not build UI that assumes a read model will be populated.
- When you do register, use the package name as the `identifier`; re-registering the same identifier unregisters the prior factory first, so registration is idempotent.

Related but separate: a factory that *throws* is caught, logged as `Factory '<id>' failed for drive '<driveId>'`, and skipped for that drive — registration does not crash.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/01-Reactor/05-Processors.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: Connect logs a warning and skips registration on the worker path, so worker-hosted reactors run no processors today.
